title: Fractional IO blended-floor experiment for Hosted API
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Hypothesis: A blended-floor that charges a small fractional minimum across combined input+output tokens (rather than separate full-direction minimums) will reduce churn for low-volume streaming customers and reduce billing disputes for enterprise buyers while preserving revenue from heavy-output use cases.

Goals and success metrics:
- Primary metric: delta in net MRR from cohort (relative to control) over 30 days as measured by signed usage-weighted revenue (goal: >= +5% net MRR within pilot cohort).
- Secondary metrics: reduction in invoices flagged for manual review (goal: -40%), change in median cost-per-response for conversational workloads, and change in streaming latency-induced retries (safeguard).
- Customer outcome: measured NPS uplift on B2B trial customers that opt into the blended-floor option.

Experiment design:
- Variants: Control (current per-direction minimums) vs Variant A (blended-floor set to 0.25x of combined IO tokens rounded to nearest 1k tokens) vs Variant B (blended-floor with soft cap + 14-day grace credit).
- Sampling: Random assign at account-level for newly billable usage over a 6-week window. Enterprise customers on active contracts are excluded unless they opt into the pilot via solutions engineering.
- Billing implementation: backend flag toggles host-side metering; billing lambda uses combined-token aggregation per-interval and applies blended-floor during invoice generation. See implementation doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PRIC/Blended+Floor+Implementation (internal).

Telemetry & dashboards:
- Primary dashboard: Looker dashboard 'pricing_experiments.blended_floor_v1' for per-account revenue and disputes.
- Latency/Retry signals: console trace:route-telemetry -> identify any correlation between floor application and keepalive/retry loops.
- QA: use synthetic workload generator (github: redwood/bench/genstream#pr-478) to validate edge cases on streaming resume.

Customer-facing considerations:
- Contract language: create an addendum template for enterprise SQ/contract teams clarifying that blended-floor will be presented as a single line-item that may reduce directional detail; legal to confirm for customers requiring separate ingress/egress reporting.
- Security questionnaire impact: ops/security requested an FAQ explaining meter calc and KMS/HSM handling of invoice proofs; coordinate with Security to add a blurb for security questionnaires under 'Billing & Metering' section.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: High-output workloads (heavy generation) might see subtle price decreases that could cannibalize revenue. Mitigation: cap blended-floor credits for accounts exceeding 95th percentile output delta and fall back to per-direction min.
- Risk: Contract disputes for customers expecting line-item IO separation. Mitigation: enterprise opt-in and explicit invoice breakdown toggles for reporting exports.

Rollout plan:
- Week 0: implement flag + internal QA and synthetic tests (ENG-xxxxx PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/4982).
- Week 1-2: internal dogfood with platform team + 5 low-risk customers (SE-managed).
- Week 3-6: ramp to randomized control trial for self-serve accounts (approx 5k accounts) and collect telemetry.
- Decision gate at Week 6: proceed to broader rollout if primary metric target met and no high-severity telem signals.

Artifacts and links:
- Proposal & rationale: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PRIC/Fractional+Blended+Floor+Proposal
- Implementation spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PRIC/Blended+Floor+Implementation
- Bench PR (load tests): https://github.com/redwood/bench/pull/478
